## Learning goals

- I can use layers, text, shapes, images, and simple effects in Photopea.
- I can choose three emotions that fit an audience.
- I can use colour, type, images, and layout to create a feeling.
- I can save an editable PSD and export a finished PNG.

## Why this is useful

A personal brand helps people understand what you make and what you care about. The same Photopea skills are used for banners, thumbnails, posters, portfolio pages, and social media graphics.

## What you will make

You will make two small deliverables:

1. **Photopea First Build:** a guided practice graphic that proves you can use the main tools.
2. **Personal Brand Graphic:** one polished banner, thumbnail, logo, or another screen graphic designed for a specific audience and built around three emotions.

## Before you start

- Open [Photopea](https://www.photopea.com/) in a new tab.
- Keep this lesson open beside it.
- Make a folder in Google Drive for your PSD and PNG files.
- Use this filename pattern: `studentnumber-lastname-project.filetype`.

Example: `123456789-Smith-photopea-first-build.psd`

## 1. Learn the interface by building

Watch the [Photopea beginner crash course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6dwSRbkSuq8). Pause often and copy the actions in your own file.

The video shows the interface, text, images, layers, masks, blend modes, adjustments, layer styles, and exporting. Do not only watch. Keep Photopea open and build while the video plays.

### Make your Photopea First Build

1. Choose **File > New**.
2. Set the canvas to **1920 px × 1080 px**, as demonstrated in the video.
3. Add a background colour.
4. Place one image that you are allowed to use.
5. Add your name or a short title.
6. Add one visible adjustment or layer style.
7. Name at least four layers so another person can understand the file.
8. Choose **File > Save as PSD**.
9. Choose **File > Export as > PNG**.

### Checkpoint 1: submit the practice files

Submit both files:

- `studentnumber-lastname-photopea-first-build.psd`
- `studentnumber-lastname-photopea-first-build.png`

This is a skills checkpoint. It is not your final personal-brand graphic.

## 2. Choose an audience and three emotions

Decide who should notice your graphic. Examples include a future employer, a co-op supervisor, a client, a club, or a creative community.

Choose **three emotions** you want that audience to feel. Use specific words when you can. For example, change *happy* to *energized*, *welcomed*, or *proud*.

For each emotion, write one design move that could create it:

| Emotion | A design move that could create it |
|---|---|
| 1. | Colour, type, image, shape, spacing, or contrast |
| 2. | Colour, type, image, shape, spacing, or contrast |
| 3. | Colour, type, image, shape, spacing, or contrast |

## 3. Choose what you want to make

After the crash course, choose **one** short build-first tutorial. Make a banner, thumbnail, logo, or another screen graphic inspired by the tutorial. Follow the techniques, then change the result so it serves your audience and your three emotions.

- [Gaming or Roblox character logo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mchoizRTY-s)
- [Apex Legends thumbnail](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t9V6Wp_OnQk)
- [Make a YouTube logo in under five minutes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QmB14oyGWcw)

The tutorial is a starting point. Your final graphic must use your own words, images, colours, and design choices. It should not be a copy of the example.

## 4. Build the first personal-brand version

1. Choose a canvas size that fits what you are making. Use the tutorial's size or an appropriate Photopea preset for a banner, thumbnail, or logo graphic.
2. Add the most important message first.
3. Add only the images and shapes that support that message.
4. Use colour and type to support all three emotions.
5. Name the important layers.
6. Save the working PSD before you continue.

### Checkpoint 2: show your direction

Show one work-in-progress screenshot or PNG. Include:

- your audience;
- your three emotions;
- one design move you used for each emotion;
- one question you want feedback on.

## 5. Test and improve

Ask one person to look at the graphic for five seconds. Do not explain it first.

Ask:

1. What did you notice first?
2. What three feelings did you get?
3. What was hard to read or understand?

Make at least one clear revision based on the feedback.

## Check your work

- The canvas size fits the banner, thumbnail, logo, or other screen graphic you chose.
- The most important idea is easy to notice.
- The text is readable at normal screen size.
- The colour contrast is strong enough to read.
- The images, type, shapes, and spacing support the three emotions.
- The PSD still has editable, clearly named layers.
- The work is your own transformation, not a copied tutorial result.

## Save, export, and submit

Submit:

- `studentnumber-lastname-personal-brand.psd`
- `studentnumber-lastname-personal-brand.png`
- your audience and three emotions;
- the feedback you received;
- the revision you made;
- a short reflection: *Which design choice best communicates your personal brand, and why?*

{{< include _rename-downloaded-file.qmd >}}

## Common issues

**My PNG is blank or missing an image.**  
Make sure the layer is visible before you export.

**My text is hard to read.**  
Increase the size, simplify the font, or use colours with stronger contrast.

**My file is one flat layer.**  
Open the PSD you saved while working. A PNG is a finished image and does not keep the same editable layers.

**I followed the tutorial exactly.**  
Change the audience, words, colours, images, type, and layout until the result communicates your three emotions.

## Summary

You learned the Photopea interface by making a small practice file. You then chose a tutorial and used an audience and three emotions to guide a banner, thumbnail, logo, or another personal-brand graphic. Keep both the PSD and PNG: the PSD proves how you built it, and the PNG is the finished image people will see.

Next: [Combine a logo and nameplate](03-combine-logo-nameplate.qmd), or use the finished graphic in your portfolio website.
